runtime_boundary: Represents the MLC LLM package, its conversion and compilation tooling, and the MLCEngine runtime, distributed as the Python package, CLI, REST server, and iOS/Android SDKs built from this repository. It is not Apache TVM, the general-purpose tensor compiler and TensorIR stack it is built on and installs as a separate dependency; TVM supplies the code generation, while this record covers the model definitions, quantization schemes, engine, and serving surfaces layered above it. It is also not WebLLM: mlc-ai/web-llm is a separately maintained, versioned, and licensed package with its own record that runs MLCEngine inside a browser through WebGPU; both consume the same compiled MLC model format, but only mlc-ai/mlc-llm's own release is scored here. The iOS and Android chat applications built from this repository are demonstrations of the SDKs, not an assistant workspace, so the project stays on the runtime side of the ADR 015 test.
model_management: A model reference of the form HF://org/repo resolves against the Hugging Face Hub, downloading pre-quantized weights into a local cache and compiling a model library on first use, after which both are reused. Custom models go through mlc_llm convert_weight to quantize a Hugging Face checkpoint into the project's own sharded parameter format, mlc_llm gen_config to emit mlc-chat-config.json and process tokenizers, and mlc_llm compile to produce the platform binary; the result can be uploaded back to the Hub. Packaging tooling bundles libraries and weights into iOS and Android application builds. There is no pinning, listing, or removal command for cached artifacts.
hardware_requirements: The project's platform table documents AMD, NVIDIA, and Intel GPUs on Linux and Windows through Vulkan, with ROCm and CUDA as vendor backends; Apple and Intel GPUs on macOS through Metal; and Apple A-series GPUs on iOS and iPadOS through Metal, plus Adreno and Mali GPUs on Android through OpenCL. The server accepts a device string of cuda, metal, vulkan, rocm, opencl, or auto. There is no documented CPU-only execution path, and compiling for a new target requires the TVM compiler installed alongside the package.
operational_controls: The server takes one of three preset engine modes — interactive, local, and server — which set maximum concurrent sequences, total sequence length, and prefill chunk size, each overridable individually along with tensor-parallel shards, GPU memory utilization, prefix-cache recycling, context or sliding-window size, and attention-sink size. Speculative decoding is selected per launch as small-draft, Eagle, or Medusa with an additional draft model. Per-request event logging is enabled with a tracing flag, and CORS origins, methods, headers, and credentials are configurable. There is no authentication, metrics endpoint, or health endpoint.
strengths: One compiler and one engine target an unusually wide set of execution surfaces — desktop GPUs on three operating systems plus iOS and Android phones — with the same OpenAI-compatible interface on each.

Compilation is a first-class, documented workflow: weight conversion, quantization configuration, model-library compilation, packaging for mobile builds, and defining a new model architecture each have their own reference page.
The server exposes tensor-parallel sharding, prefix caching, configurable batch sizing through engine modes, and three families of speculative decoding without requiring a separate orchestrator.
tradeoffs: Nothing runs without conversion and compilation: weights must be transformed into the project's own quantized shard format and paired with a compiled model library for the exact target, so a stock checkpoint cannot be pointed at and served directly.
Operational visibility is minimal, with per-request tracing and a CLI statistics command but no metrics endpoint, health endpoint, authentication, container image, or orchestration guidance.

The supported model architecture list is narrower than mainstream server engines, and the published documentation is still versioned 0.1.0 with pages of differing freshness, so capability must be confirmed per model and per release.
license_note: The repository publishes a single verbatim Apache-2.0 license file covering the compiler, engine, and tooling. The accompanying NOTICE file carries only the project name and a contributor copyright line and imposes no additional terms. The Apache TVM dependency is installed separately and is not vendored into this repository.
